newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Telkom sale may net 5-6 bln rand.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Telkom sale may net 5-6 bln rand.

text.p: The sale of a 30 percent strategic equity stake in state utility Telkom could raise five to six billion rand in cash, officials said on Thursday.
"Five to six billion rand is the cash component. The value could go to seven billion rand," postmaster general Andile Ngcaba told reporters.
He said negotiations would cover injections of technology training and equipment that could boost the value of the equity partnership.

Post and telecommunications minister Jay Naidoo said the 10 percent equity share that would be made available for black empowerment was not a condition of union support for the restructuring deal, but was in line with government policy.
"The nature of the empowerment deal is subject to further negotiation, but I would not like to rule out any option that would take us further...including a (share price) discount," he said.
Naidoo said the government would like to deliver an equity stake directly to black investors, including Telkom staff, adding: "We are looking for creative solutions."
Negotiations with the partnership candidates would include ideas to make telephone services affordable to blacks disadvantaged under apartheid.

The cost of domestic telephone services would be subsidised by corporate and so-called value-added services. The government's plan to double the number of telephone lines by the turn of the century would be amongst the obligations taken on by the Telkom's new partners, he said.
